title: Bind repaired pending manifests to payload SHA-256 proof
summary: Align Python pending-manifest validation and orphan repair with the PowerShell drain's mandatory SHA-256 byte-proof contract.
reason: Remediate P1 AUDIT-FIND-W15-001. The Python current-manifest contract accepts missing output hash proof, so strict orphan reconcile can report success and write a manifest that the unchanged PowerShell drain rejects as OUTPUT_HASH_MISSING.
affected_areas: orphan payload reconcile dry-run and apply
behavior_before: A current pending_push_manifest.v1 proposal could omit output_sha256 and output_hash_algorithm, pass Python dry-run/apply, and be materialized even though the drain must reject it.
behavior_after: Current Python manifests require SHA-256 proof, orphan reconcile verifies that proof against the selected payload during dry-run and again immediately before apply, and hashless or stale proposals remain blocked without writing a manifest.
tests_added: Contract tests require media and sidecar size/SHA-256 proof and compare Python acceptance with the actual PowerShell current-manifest validator.
Repair dry-run tests reject hashless media, same-shape stale media proof, and stale sidecar proof; apply tests reject a same-size payload mutation after dry-run without writing a manifest.
The existing local-API orphan repair integration now proves that an applied Python repair is accepted and published by the unchanged PowerShell drain.
manual_validation: The exact AUDIT-FIND-W15-001 reproduction failed before the correction because Python apply succeeded but the unchanged PowerShell drain left the output unpublished; the same integration passes after the correction.
Changed production Python compiled successfully; targeted Ruff lint passed without bulk-formatting legacy files.
Focused contract validation passed 7 tests with 28 subtests; focused repair validation passed 33 tests with 5 subtests; the critical proof/revalidation slice passed 3 tests with 2 subtests.
The widened pending-publish Python/WebView slice passed 167 tests with 56 subtests, and the synthetic WebView real-media smoke passed 2 tests.
Cross-language Python-to-PowerShell contract parity passed for a fully proved manifest and for rejection of missing media proof with OUTPUT_HASH_MISSING.

Invoke-PendingPublishSafetyChecks.ps1 and Invoke-PendingPublishTransactionFaultInjectionChecks.ps1 passed, including hash-bound sidecars, tamper prevention, crash seams, retry, and idempotency coverage.

Generated-context/tooling validation passed 44 tests with 72 subtests; architecture guardrails, risky-file registry, naming lint, and feature-map check passed. The god-file guard reported 0 errors and 57 warnings across 376 candidates, including existing size warnings for the touched repair modules.

The failure-code registry remains red only on the independently audited W15-002 cluster: OUTPUT_HASH_MISSING, SIDECAR_HASH_INVALID, and SIDECAR_SIZE_INVALID. This packet does not claim that registry debt as fixed.

Active-doc validation remains red only on unrelated DOC005 in the immutable audit baseline reference; summary freshness remains red only on five unrelated known stale files after refreshing this packet.

No representative real-media validation was run. It remains advisable before release, but is not required for this fail-closed validation-only correction because drain movement and final-placement policy were not changed.
rollback_plan: Revert the Python contract, dry-run/apply proof checks, fixtures/tests, generated context, and this packet together. Do not weaken the unchanged PowerShell drain hash requirement independently.
notes: High-risk pending-publish boundary reviewed. This packet does not edit drain execution, move source media, or weaken manifest trust. Required validation: focused Python contract/dry-run/apply tests, unchanged PowerShell pending safety and transaction fault-injection suites, cross-language synthetic repair-then-drain with unchanged source bytes, generated-context checks, and strict packet coverage. Representative real-media validation is advisable before release but is not required for this fail-closed validation-only correction because final-placement policy and drain movement code are unchanged.
